title: Environmental Chemistry: Pollution, Climate, and Green Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
questions.rationale: Ground-level ozone is not emitted directly; it forms in the air when sunlight acts on NOx and hydrocarbons — that makes it secondary.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide is poisonous because:
options: It binds haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen
It destroys vitamin K in the blood
questions.rationale: CO's grip on haemoglobin is roughly 200 times oxygen's, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and starving the body of oxygen.

questions.question: Clean water has a BOD value:
questions.rationale: BOD under about 5 ppm indicates little organic load; values above roughly 100 ppm signal heavy pollution — microbes are consuming lots of oxygen.

questions.question: Eutrophication of a lake is triggered chiefly by:
options: Nitrogen and phosphorus runoff causing algal blooms
questions.rationale: Fertiliser nutrients feed an algal bloom; when the algae die and decompose, dissolved oxygen crashes and aquatic life suffocates.

questions.question: Biomagnification of DDT in a food chain means its concentration:
options: Breaks down faster at each level
Concentrates as it moves up to higher trophic levels
questions.rationale: DDT is persistent and fat-soluble, so it accumulates and multiplies at each step up the chain — famously thinning birds' eggshells.

questions.question: The largest share of man-made greenhouse gas emissions (by CO₂-equivalent) is:
questions.rationale: CO₂ contributes about 76% of emissions in CO₂-equivalent terms, ahead of methane (~16%), N₂O (~6%) and F-gases (~2%).

questions.question: How does a single chlorine atom released from a CFC damage the ozone layer?
options: It reacts once and is consumed
It acts as a catalyst, destroying thousands of ozone molecules
It reflects UV radiation back to space
It converts ozone into new CFCs
questions.rationale: In the cycle Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂ and ClO + O → Cl + O₂, the chlorine returns untouched to strike again — a catalyst of destruction.

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol, which phased out CFCs, was signed in:
questions.rationale: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 — the first treaty ratified by every UN member — drove the global CFC phase-out that is healing the ozone layer.

questions.question: Rain is called acid rain when its pH is:
questions.rationale: Natural rain is already slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6) from dissolved CO₂; SO₂ and NOₓ push the pH below this, forming H₂SO₄ and HNO₃.

questions.question: The central idea of green chemistry is to:
options: Design products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances from the start
Bury all waste in deep landfills
questions.rationale: Green chemistry prevents pollution at the design stage — waste prevention, atom economy, safer solvents, catalysis — instead of cleaning up later.
